problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $CD=DC={I}_{3}$
- $CE=EC={I}_{3}$
- $E={C}^{-1}$
worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $CD=DC={I}_{3}.$ Computing $CD$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}CD & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $DC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}DC & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is true.

- Now, we check whether $CE=EC={I}_{3}.$ Computing $CE$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}CE & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{3}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is false. As a result, $E\ne {C}^{-1}$ and statement III is false too.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
